item.title: CME Group To Launch World's First Baseball Futures On October 12
item.content:encoded:
• New contracts will be based on CME FutureSports Performance Indexes tracking Official League Data

CME Group, the world's leading derivatives marketplace, today announced it will launch the world's first Baseball futures on October 12, pending regulatory review. The new contracts will track CME FutureSports Performance Indexes (CME FSPI) that include statistics on the 30 professional baseball teams, beginning with the 2026 Postseason and the four clubs in the League Championship Series.

"CME Group provides price discovery and risk management across every major investable asset class, and we see an opportunity to bring investing and hedging discipline to the business of professional baseball," said Tim McCourt, Senior Managing Director and Global Head of Equities, FX and Alternative Products at CME Group. "The innovative contracts we're developing with FutureSports will be built on robust indexes using Official League Data, with the transparency and integrity that only regulated exchange-traded products deliver."

CME Group Baseball futures will be available in standard-sized contracts, valued at 10x the underlying CME FSPI MLB indexes, and micro-sized contracts that are 1/10 the value of those indexes. Participants can trade live around the clock, allowing for immediate positions on a regulated exchange with central clearing safeguards, transparent pricing and equal market access.

CME FSPI structure official sports statistics into rules-based, benchmark financial metrics. The performance of the indexes will be calculated using systematic methodologies where point allocations follow transparent statistical frameworks – adding points for positive actions and subtracting for negative plays or setbacks.

The CME FSPI methodologies align with the International Organization of Securities Commissions (IOSCO) Principles for Financial Benchmarks and are supported by published governance and oversight procedures.

CME Group Baseball futures are listed on and subject to the rules of CME. For more information, visit cmegroup.com/fspi.

item.title: Report From FINRA Board Of Governors’ September Meeting - Board Approves Four Rule Proposals As Part Of FINRA Forward Rule Modernization
item.content:encoded:
At its meeting Sept. 29-30, the FINRA Board of Governors approved four rule proposals for filing with the SEC and received briefings on key initiatives, including FINRA's ongoing rule modernization efforts.

The rule proposals reflect stakeholder feedback received through FINRA Forward, an ongoing effort to improve FINRA's effectiveness and efficiency in pursuing its mission of investor protection and market integrity.

"These rule proposals underscore FINRA's continued commitment to refreshing the regulatory framework applicable to member firms, markets and investors. They focus membership application reviews more closely on risk, provide greater flexibility in meeting certification deadlines and eliminate an outdated quoting requirement, among other improvements. Together, they illustrate how FINRA is taking meaningful steps to enhance efficiencies while preserving the investor protections that are central to FINRA's mission," said FINRA Board Chair Scott Curtis.

Rulemaking

The following rule proposals will be filed with the SEC:

  • Membership Application Review: The proposal would amend rules governing FINRA's review of new and continuing membership applications to better focus on risk.
  • CEO Certification Deadline Flexibility: The proposal would make the annual CEO compliance and supervisory processes certification deadline more flexible.
  • Rescission of the Same Quote Rule: The proposal would rescind the Same Quote Rule requiring members to display the same price for any over-the-counter equity security that they quote across multiple platforms. 
  • Mutual Fund Cash Compensation Disclosure: The proposal would repeal a mutual fund prospectus cash compensation disclosure requirement in light of its overlap with the SEC’s Regulation Best Interest and other disclosure rules.

Information about FINRA's current priorities, active rule filings and recently approved or immediately effective rule filings is detailed in the FINRA Quarterly Regulatory Policy Agenda.

Governance and Oversight

The Board received several briefings on key initiatives as part of its oversight of management and the administration of FINRA's work. These included updates on FINRA's AI strategy, market surveillance program, cyber and information security program, rule modernization initiative and the recent integration of several teams into a unified Regulatory Operations division.

Executive Vice President and Head of Enforcement Bill St. Louis briefed the Board on steps FINRA is taking to address recommendations from the recent external review of the Enforcement Program. The briefing is part of our response to the report’s call for FINRA to engage the Board in more frequent discussions on the program. With budget planning for 2027 underway, the Board received updates on FINRA's finances, including recent measures to address surplus reserves.

More information about the Board's operations, including its membership and the responsibilities of its committees, is available here.

item.title: EDX Markets And VerifiedX Partner To Bring Verified Bitcoin (vBTC) To Institutional Markets - Partnership Will Bring vBTC To EDX Markets For Institutional Spot Trading, While EDX Joins The VerifiedX Network As A Validator, Expanding Institutional Access To Tokenized, Programmable And Self-Custodial Bitcoin Infrastructure
item.content:encoded:
VerifiedX (verifiedx.io), the programmable financial operating system for Bitcoin and intel assets, and EDX Markets (“EDX”), a leading digital asset technology firm that combines institution-only trading venue with a central clearinghouse, announced a strategic partnership to bring Verified Bitcoin (vBTC), a tokenized form of Bitcoin, to EDX for institutional spot trading.

Unlike conventional Bitcoin products, which rely on synthetic exposure or passive custody, vBTC is designed to activate Bitcoin as programmable, self-custodial capital while maintaining 1:1 underlying Bitcoin collateralization and native redemption liquidity back to Bitcoin at all times. As part of the partnership, EDX will join the VerifiedX network as a validator, providing EDX with direct participation in network validation and governance while extending the relationship beyond asset trading into the underlying infrastructure supporting vBTC. The
partnership represents a significant expansion of institutional market infrastructure for Bitcoin connecting EDX’s institutional trading and clearing ecosystem with VerifiedX’s Bitcoin-nation financial infrastructure.

From Bitcoin Exposure to Bitcoin Infrastructure

Bitcoin has become a globally recognized institutional asset, yet much of its financial utility remains fragmented across exchanges, custodians, wrappers, bridges and application-layer protocols. VerifiedX has addressed that fragmentation with vBTC, enabling Bitcoin to remain verifiably backed on-chain while becoming programmable across trading, payments, treasury management, lending and other financial applications.

The collaboration is expected to support a range of institutional strategies, including:

  • Bitcoin trading and price discovery through institutional spot markets;
  • Cross-market arbitrage and liquidity strategies between BTC and vBTC markets;
  • Treasury and balance-sheet mobility, allowing Bitcoin capital to move between trading and programmable environments;
  • Borrowing, lending and yield strategies built around Bitcoin-backed capital;
  • On-chain liquidity and financial applications native to VerifiedX; and
  • EVM composability through vBTC.b, the canonical representation of vBTC for supported EVM environments, allowing Bitcoin capital to participate in broader decentralized financial markets while preserving a direct redemption path to underlying Bitcoin.

Every vBTC represents Bitcoin collateralized 1:1 by underlying BTC, with Taproot addresses embedded in each token, and is designed with an evergreen redemption path back to native Bitcoin. Rather than creating economic exposure to Bitcoin without a direct path to the underlying asset, vBTC is built around continuous ownership, utilization and redemption.

Through EDX, market participants will gain a new venue for trading vBTC within an institutional market structure designed around aggregated liquidity, central clearing and capital-efficient settlement.

The objective is straightforward: allow Bitcoin to move between holding, trading, settlement and utilization without requiring allocators to surrender the fundamental economic relationship between the asset they deploy and the underlying Bitcoin they own.

Building an Institutional Market Around Programmable Bitcoin

“Bitcoin does not need another financial abstraction. It needs infrastructure that allows the asset itself to do more,” said Jay Pollak, Head of Strategy at the VerifiedX Foundation. “Bringing vBTC to EDX is important because it connects programmable Bitcoin capital with market infrastructure purpose-built for sophisticated institutions. An allocator should be able to trade Bitcoin, deploy it, move it across financial environments and ultimately redeem back to Bitcoin without losing the fundamental ownership characteristics that made Bitcoin valuable in the first place.”

“EDX joining as a validator makes this partnership even more meaningful. This is not simply about adding another trading pair. It connects institutional trading infrastructure directly with the network infrastructure underneath the asset. Institutions can also operate their own validators and control their own threshold signing, eliminating the requirement to depend on a public signing pool. We believe that combination of liquidity, programmability, institutional control and evergreen Bitcoin redemption is an important step toward Bitcoin becoming active programmable financial infrastructure,” added Pollak.

“Institutional adoption of digital assets increasingly depends on giving sophisticated market participants greater flexibility in how they trade, move and deploy capital,” said David Olsson, Chief Commercial Officer of EDX Markets. “Our work with VerifiedX is intended to expand the infrastructure available to institutional Bitcoin participants by connecting EDX’s trading and clearing capabilities with an asset designed for broader programmability and mobility.”

Institutional Control Without Dependence on a Public Signing Pool

A core component of the VerifiedX architecture is the ability for institutional allocators to establish their own validator infrastructure and control the threshold-signing environment associated with their Bitcoin.

Institutions are not required to rely exclusively on the VerifiedX public validator pool.

Any allocator can operate its own VerifiedX validators, register its vBTC environment to its own threshold-signing configuration and maintain institutional control over the signing infrastructure governing its Bitcoin ingress and redemption.

This architecture is intended to give institutions a fundamentally different choice: access programmable Bitcoin infrastructure while retaining direct operational control over the infrastructure securing their underlying Bitcoin at all times.

A New Market Structure for Bitcoin Capital

EDX is purpose-built for institutional digital asset trading and operates a spot trading venue with a central clearinghouse designed to reduce bilateral counterparty exposure and improve capital and operational efficiency. The collaboration with VerifiedX allows firms to utilize vBTC across a wider range of financial workflows while maintaining native ownership and a direct path back to the underlying asset.

For Bitcoin allocators, the addition of vBTC creates a potential bridge between two historically separate environments: institutional market structure and programmable digital-asset infrastructure.

Bitcoin as Native Financial Infrastructure

The EDX and VerifiedX partnership reflects a broader evolution in institutional Bitcoin markets.

The first phase of institutional adoption established Bitcoin as an asset that could be bought, held and traded. The next phase is about what that capital can do, and tokenized Bitcoin is how it does it.

VerifiedX has built the infrastructure intended to allow Bitcoin to operate as an active financial asset across markets without requiring institutions to accept unnecessary layers of synthetic exposure, opaque intermediaries or permanent disconnection from native Bitcoin liquidity.

The combination of EDX’s institutional trading infrastructure with VerifiedX’s programmable Bitcoin architecture is intended to create a more complete lifecycle for institutional Bitcoin capital — from execution and liquidity to ownership, settlement, programmability and redemption.

Additional details regarding vBTC and EDX will be announced in the coming weeks.

item.title: Canadian Securities Regulators Publish Final Amendments Prohibiting Chargebacks In Investment Fund Distribution
item.content:encoded:
The Canadian Securities Administrators (CSA) today announced the publication of final amendments to National Instrument 31-103 Registration Requirements, Exemptions and Ongoing Registrant Obligations prohibiting chargebacks in publicly offered investment fund distribution. The changes are intended to improve investor protection and help maintain investor confidence in Canada’s capital markets.

Dealers or dealing representatives sometimes receive an upfront commission or payment when their client purchases securities. Chargebacks occur when clients redeem their securities before a fixed schedule, and the dealing representative is required to repay all or part of the upfront commission or payment.

The CSA is concerned that the use of chargebacks creates a significant conflict of interest because they may incentivize advisors to prioritize their own financial interests over those of their clients.

“By prohibiting chargebacks in the distribution of investment fund securities, we are removing a compensation structure that can create conflicts between an advisor’s interests and those of their clients,” said Stan Magidson, CSA Chair and Chair and CEO of the Alberta Securities Commission. “The changes will help protect investors by better aligning investment advice and foster fairer compensation practices.”

The CSA, the council of the securities regulators of Canada’s provinces and territories, coordinates and harmonizes regulation for the Canadian capital markets.

The BC Securities Commission did not participate in this news release due to publication restrictions related to the upcoming B.C. provincial election.

item.title: ESMA Sets Out Supervisory Expectations On Services Related To Unauthorised Stablecoins
item.content:encoded:
The European Securities and Markets Authority (ESMA), the EU regulator and supervisor, has published an opinion clarifying supervisory expectations of crypto-asset services involving asset-referenced tokens (ARTs) and e-money tokens (EMTs) - also known as stablecoins- that do not comply with the requirements of the Markets in Crypto-Assets Regulation (MiCA).

Crypto-asset service providers (CASPs) authorised under MiCA should cease providing services related to non-MiCA-compliant stablecoins to clients in the European Union.

This applies to the full range of crypto-asset services covered by MiCA, including the operation of trading platforms, exchange services, execution of orders, placing of crypto-assets, reception and transmission of orders, investment advice, transfers, custody and administration, and portfolio management, whether these services are provided individually or in combination.

The opinion calls on National Competent Authorities (NCAs) to supervise that market participants neither maintain, introduce, nor facilitate access for clients to non-MiCA-compliant stablecoins through their services. NCAs should also ensure that CASPs implement appropriate technical, contractual, and organisational controls to prevent the availability of such tokens in the European Union, including controls preventing clients from acquiring or increasing exposures to those tokens. 

Next steps

When NCAs identify remaining pre-existing exposures, they should require their remediation as soon as possible and no later than three months after the publication of the opinion. 

Any continuation of services should be strictly limited to activities necessary for the liquidation, conversion, withdrawal, transfer or safekeeping of such assets, and should remain time-limited, risk-based, and closely supervised.

item.title: TMX Group Equity Financing Statistics – September 2026 - Toronto Stock Exchange, TSX Venture Exchange
item.content:encoded:
TMX Group today announced its financing activity on Toronto Stock Exchange (TSX) and TSX Venture Exchange (TSXV) for September 2026.

TSX welcomed 28 new issuers in September 2026, compared with 14 in the previous month and 29 in September 2025. The new listings were 27 exchange traded funds and one mining company. Total financings raised in September 2026 decreased 36% compared to the previous month, but were up 263% compared to September 2025. The total number of financings in September 2026 was 53, compared with 29 the previous month and 55 in September 2025.

There were 88 financings in September 2026, compared with 77 in the previous month and 119 in September 2025.

item.title: Industry Leaders Warn Firms Must Act Now Ahead Of T+1 Deadline
item.content:encoded:
With one year to go until the UK and EU transition to T+1 settlement, industry experts are urging firms to move beyond automation and focus on exception management, data infrastructure, and the road to atomic settlement.

As the deadline approaches, two senior voices in the post-trade space have outlined the key challenges firms must address in the coming months.

Exception Management Must Take Centre Stage

James Maxfield, Chief Client Officer at Duco, argues that while automation has dominated much of the conversation around T+1 readiness, firms risk overlooking a critical piece of the puzzle: what happens when things go wrong.

"Zero exceptions is an admirable goal but highly unrealistic," Maxfield warned. "Firms need to go beyond automating post-trade activities like allocation and address the question of who, or what, is in charge when something doesn't match up at 22:00 on trade date, and how fast they can act."

Maxfield points to the growing use of 24/7 AI agents as a promising solution, with some firms already deploying them to investigate and resolve exceptions in real time - reducing the risk of activity spikes and enabling firms to manage exceptions at scale.

"T+1 will not be the end point either," he added. "The work that firms do now to build smarter post-trade operations will also put them in a much stronger position for any future move towards T0."

Fragmented Data Poses a Critical Risk

Richard Baker, Founder and CEO of Tokenovate, highlights a separate but equally pressing concern: the state of firms' data and infrastructure.

According to Tokenovate's latest research, only 32% of respondents say their organisations are fully prepared with compatible workflows, systems, and operations already in place. More strikingly, 88% identified fragmented data as a significant or critical challenge to post-trade efficiency.

"Fragmented data, manual hand-offs and exceptions are already a challenge," Baker said. "With significantly less time to resolve them, they will become a much bigger problem."
Baker urges firms to use the T+1 transition as an opportunity to join up automation across the trade lifecycle, standardise transaction and event data, and keep the legal and economic terms of a trade connected through to settlement.

Eyes Already on Atomic Settlement

Both executives agree that T+1 is not the finish line. Tokenovate's research suggests the industry expects widespread atomic settlement in the UK within an average of 3.7 years — meaning the infrastructure decisions firms make today will have long-lasting consequences.

"Common standards will be essential to ensuring those systems can interoperate across the market," Baker noted. "The changes being made today need to support a future where cash, assets and obligations can move together across different infrastructures."

With twelve months to go, the message from both leaders is clear: the time to act is now.

item.title: EACH Calls For A Better Supervisory System And Positive Progress Through MISP
item.content:encoded:
Ahead of this Friday’s ECOFIN Council meeting, EACH has published a statement calling for an agreement on the Market Integration and Supervision Package (MISP) that delivers a more effective, efficient and proportionate supervisory system. We support the objectives of removing barriers and unlocking the potential of EU capital markets. Reform should simplify supervision and improve competitiveness, without adding complexity or disproportionate costs as follows:

  • An efficient and independent ESMA Executive Board - The success of the reform will ultimately depend on the Executive Board being able to exercise genuine supervisory authority and take decisions efficiently and independently at EU level. While we understand the desire of some Member States to retain an oversight role through the Board of Supervisors, it is important that the final framework preserves a clear allocation of responsibilities within ESMA. The Executive Board should be able to exercise its supervisory powers independently and efficiently, while the Board of Supervisors provides appropriate oversight without creating overlapping decision-making processes or undermining accountability for supervisory outcomes.
  • A workable permanent model - The final framework must demonstrate practical improvements in supervisory efficiency, authorisations and approvals, while preserving financial stability and supporting innovation and competitiveness.
  • No Joint Supervisory Teams or comparable structures - We oppose JSTs. We recognise authorities’ need to remain informed, but this should be addressed through clear information-sharing and cooperation arrangements. JSTs may represent a step backwards by duplicating supervision, increasing costs and weakening accountability.
  • A clear and short transition - Responsibilities must be defined at every stage, including when they transfer to ESMA. The transition should minimise disruption and avoid overlapping requirements or temporary supervisory layers.
  • Proportionate supervisory fees - Fees should be transparent and reflect efficiently delivered supervisory tasks. CCPs should not bear disproportionate charges for duplicated activities, overlapping structures or avoidable transition costs.
  • Effective crisis management - Supervision, crisis coordination and resolution responsibilities must be clearly distinguished. Additional measures should only be considered if they address demonstrated gaps in existing CCP safeguards.
  • Beyond supervision, towards more competitive ecosystem – In addition, to make the EU clearing ecosystem more competitive, regulatory burdens could be significantly reduced by simplifying reporting and outsourcing requirements, innovation enabled by providing legal certainty regarding the use of DLT and clearing incentivised by addressing regulatory hurdles faced by asset managers when accessing CCPs.

Please find the statement here.

For more information visit the EACH website.

item.title: Corporate CUSIP Request Volumes Rise In September - Municipal Volumes Edge Higher
item.content:encoded:
CUSIP Global Services (CGS) today announced the release of its CUSIP Issuance Trends Report for September 2026. The report, which tracks the issuance of new security identifiers as an early indicator of debt and capital markets activity over the next quarter, found a monthly increase in request volume for new corporate identifiers, and a modest increase in request volume for new municipal identifiers.

North American corporate CUSIP requests totaled 9,100 in September, which represents a 6.5% increase on a monthly basis. On an annualized basis, North American corporate requests were up 10.3% over September 2025 totals. Requests for new U.S. corporate debt identifiers rose 6.3% and requests for new U.S. corporate equity identifiers rose 17.6% for the month of September.

The aggregate total of identifier requests for new municipal securities – including municipal bonds, long-term and short-term notes, and commercial paper – rose 2.0% versus August totals. On a year-over-year basis, overall municipal volumes were down 1.5% through the end of September. Texas led state-level municipal request volume with a total of 184 new CUSIP requests in September, followed by New York (175) and California (104).

“September brought a clear rebound in corporate request activity, and the 17.6% monthly jump in new U.S. corporate equity identifiers is especially notable, with equity requests now running nearly 30% ahead of last year’s pace,” said Gerard Faulkner, Director of Operations for CGS. “There is clearly a glut of deal activity on the sidelines waiting for the right moment and we’re starting to see that increased pre-market activity show up in our CUSIP request volumes.”

Requests for international equity CUSIPs rose 41.6% in September and international debt CUSIP requests were up 26.6%. On an annualized basis, international equity CUSIP requests were down 0.6% and international debt CUSIP requests were up 11.5%.

item.title: Industry Marks One Year To T+1 Settlement Transition In UK, EU And Switzerland - DTCC Comment On T+1 One Year To Go Milestone
item.content:encoded:
With exactly one year to go until the UK, EU and Switzerland make the shift to T+1 settlement, industry leaders are calling on market participants to use the time wisely — not just to prepare for a shorter settlement cycle, but to drive broader transformation across the post-trade ecosystem.

Val Wotton, Managing Director and Global Head of Equities Solutions at DTCC, says the milestone is a timely reminder of what is at stake.

"T+1 is about much more than shortening the settlement cycle. It is a catalyst for change across the post-trade ecosystem," Wotton said.

According to Wotton, the transition presents a unique opportunity for firms to modernise operating models, accelerate automation, improve data quality and strengthen collaboration across markets and jurisdictions. Those that use the next 12 months to reimagine workflows and address long-standing operational inefficiencies, he argues, will be best placed for success in 2027 and beyond.
While acknowledging the significant progress already made, Wotton was clear that considerable work remains. A successful transition, he stressed, will require sustained industry-wide engagement and coordination across the full trade lifecycle.

DTCC has reaffirmed its commitment to supporting the industry through this period, citing its solutions, market expertise and ongoing collaboration with clients, policymakers and stakeholders as key pillars of that effort.

"We look forward to working with the industry over the coming year to help ensure a smooth transition and to realise the broader benefits that T+1 can unlock for capital markets," Wotton added.

item.title: ClearToken And Consensys Partner To Bring 24/7 Settlement Infrastructure To Wholesale Markets - Cryptographic Finality Meets Settlement Finality: Powerful, Regulated Infrastructure For The Movement Of Money And Assets On Chain
item.content:encoded:
ClearToken, the UK-based market infrastructure group for digital and traditional assets, and Consensys, the protocols and institutional infrastructure company, today announce a strategic partnership to help banks move tokenised assets and cash onto always-on infrastructure, with the legal certainty and controls wholesale markets require.

The partnership pairs two kinds of finality. Consensys brings cryptographic finality, the technical certainty that a transaction recorded on chain cannot be altered. ClearToken is designed to bring settlement finality, the legal certainty that a transfer of money or assets is final and irrevocable.

Markets never sleep. Post-trade infrastructure still does. A tokenised asset that can move 24/7 delivers little if it cannot clear, settle and be safeguarded on the same basis.

By combining market infrastructure being built inside the UK regulatory perimeter with proven, scalable and resilient blockchain technology, the two firms aim to give institutions a route to round-the-clock markets without compromising on control.

Key points

  • Settlement around the clock: ClearToken CSD Limited is designed to enable eligible securities held at different banks to be tokenised and recognised as a single fungible instrument, under its Gate 2 approval in the Bank of England’s Digital Securities Sandbox. Working with ClearToken Depository Limited, the group’s FCA-authorised payment institution, the aim is to settle these on a delivery-versus-payment basis against cash, including fiat, tokenised deposits and stablecoins, 24/7.

  • Interoperability: Consensys connects banks, brokers and asset managers across blockchain networks and financial market infrastructures in a safe, private and compliant manner.

  • Technology and distribution: ClearToken will draw on Consensys for scalable, resilient tokenisation infrastructure, and for the wallets and client reach to bring tokenised assets to institutional clients and partners.

Ben Santos-Stephens, CEO of ClearToken Group, said: “Wholesale markets are embracing a diverse and growing ecosystem of networks and blockchains. Realising the full potential of that ecosystem depends on infrastructure that connects the banks, assets and ledgers already in use, and works across whichever networks institutions choose to distribute cash and assets to their clients. Consensys brings the technology and the institutional relationships to deliver that at scale. We are building the legal and clearing framework institutions need in order to rely on it.”

David Cunningham, President of Consensys, said: “Financial institutions and market infrastructures are moving to always-on operations, with tokenisation at the core. Consensys is delivering interoperability for bank-issued tokens globally, across multiple payment schemes and financial market infrastructures. ClearToken is building a regulated route to clearing and settlement on a 24/7/365 basis, subject to clearing authorisation by the Bank of England. Together, this enables our clients to operate around the clock, opening up new business opportunities and reducing risk.”

Mark Williamson, Chief Commercial Officer of ClearToken Group, said: “Our clients have asked for one thing above all: tokenisation that fits into how they already manage risk and collateral. Working with Consensys puts that within reach of banks, brokers and asset managers.”

item.title: Broadridge’s Distributed Ledger Repo Processes $7.5 Trillion In September - September 2026 ADV Reaches $359 Billion As Broadridge Builds On DLR’s Institutional Scale With Newly Launched DLX
item.content:encoded:
Broadridge (NYSE: BR), global Fintech leader, today announced that its Distributed Ledger Repo (DLR) processed an average of $359 billion in daily repo transactions during September, with volumes totaling $7.5 trillion. The daily average increase demonstrates the continued scale of tokenized securities financing activity as Broadridge expands its digital asset infrastructure beyond repo through its recently launched fully integrated, end-to-end tokenization and digital asset infrastructure platform, DLX.

“DLR has demonstrated that tokenized market infrastructure can operate at the scale and consistency required for core institutional activity,” said Horacio Barakat, Global Head of Digital Innovation at Broadridge. “That real-world foundation is allowing us to take the next step with DLX, extending the infrastructure and operating experience we’ve built in repo to a broader range of assets and workflows. This makes it possible for institutions to bring tokenization into more parts of their business through infrastructure that seamlessly connects with how markets already operate.”

Building on the proven infrastructure and institutional experience behind DLR, DLX extends Broadridge’s capabilities beyond securities financing into a broader, multi-asset platform spanning issuance, trading, settlement, servicing, custody, governance and distribution. Through a modular, multi-chain architecture and common operating layer connecting traditional and on-chain activity, DLX helps financial institutions integrate tokenized assets into existing operating models while reducing operational complexity.

To learn more about DLR, the world’s largest institutional platform for settling tokenized real assets, visit Broadridge’s DLR.

About Broadridge’s Tokenization Solutions

Broadridge enables on-chain proxy voting and governance, digital asset infrastructure including post trade, wallets and custody, and the scaling of digital asset capabilities across multiple asset classes. Broadridge’s governance platform serves all models of tokenized securities, including issuer-listed models, synthetic securities issued outside the United States, and third-party tokenized shares within the United States, helping ensure investors receive the same rights and protections regardless of how assets are structured or owned.

DLX is Broadridge’s tokenization platform, designed to help financial institutions operate across the lifecycle of tokenized securities. It brings together solutions spanning issuance, trading, financing, settlement and servicing, including its Distributed Ledger Repo (DLR) solution, the world’s largest institutional platform for settling tokenized real assets, tokenizing over $359 billion a day. DLR supports repo transactions, intraday repo activity, collateral movements, settlement and servicing needs through established scale, critical market knowledge and technology designed for real-world market operations. As tokenization gains momentum across financial services, Broadridge is abstracting away the complexity and enabling a unified experience across traditional and digital assets.

item.title: UK Financial Conduct Authority: New Rules To Make Long-Term Investment Funds Clearer
item.content:encoded:
The FCA has set out clearer expectations for asset managers about long-term investments, such as property.

This will help give the market more confidence to invest in funds that support private markets.

The new rules mean that investors will have to give 90 days' notice to access their funds but will be more certain that they will receive their money.

For investors, this means the fund should be clearer from the start about how quickly they can get their money back and whether the fund is right for their needs.

Currently some of these funds allow people to take money out daily with no notice period. During periods of stress or volatility there is a risk that some funds may suspend all payments due to lack of available cash. Some are also holding extra cash, leaving less invested in their intended assets.

Rushed sales can lower prices, harm investors who stay invested and put pressure on markets.

The new notice period would give managers time to sell assets in an orderly way and make liquidity-driven suspensions less likely.

Existing funds would have 2 years to comply and give investors at least 1 year’s notice.

The proposals bring the UK into line with new international liquidity standards for open ended funds.

Michelle Beck, director, markets, at the FCA, said: 'Funds should be clear about whether they offer quick access or are built for longer-term investments like property. Our rules will help firms make that clearer and give the market more confidence to invest.'

Background

  1. Read CP26/35: Fair redemption terms for authorised funds investing in illiquid assets.
  2. The FCA is asking for feedback on the proposals by 11 December 2026.
  3. The consultation covers authorised fund managers of non-UCITS retail schemes, known as NURS. 
  4. The FCA uses the term 'inherently illiquid assets' for assets that cannot normally be sold quickly without a significant loss in value. These can include property and infrastructure investments.
  5. Fund managers could set a notice period longer than the minimum where the fund’s assets or investment strategy require it.

item.title: Non-Jordanian Ownership In Companies Listed On The Amman Stock Exchange Reached 46.0%, Of Which 32.8% For Institutional Investors
item.content:encoded:
Amman Stock Exchange (ASE) statistics revealed that the value of shares bought by non-Jordanian investors at the ASE in September 2026 was JD49.5 million, representing 15.8% of the overall trading value, while the value of shares sold by them amounted to JD37.3million.

The value of shares bought by non-Jordanian investors since the beginning of the year until the end of September 2026 was JD311.5 million, representing 12.2 % of the overall trading value, while the value of shares sold by them amounted to JD366.9 million.

Arab investors’ purchases during September 2026 were JD47.3 million, or 95.6% of the overall purchases by non-Jordanians, while their sales amounted to JD34.3 million, or 91.9% of non-Jordanians total sales. The value of non-Arab purchases amounted to JD2.2 million, constituting 4.4% of the overall purchases by non-Jordanians, while their sales value amounted to JD3.0 million, representing 8.1% of the total sales by non-Jordanians.

Hence, non-Jordanian investors' ownership in companies listed on ASE as of end of September 2026 represented 46.0% of the total market value, of which 32.8% for institutional investors including companies, institutions and funds. Arab investors own 29.6% and non-Arab investors own 16.4%. At the sectoral level, the non-Jordanian ownership in the financial sector was 47.6%, in the services sector was 22.4% and 51.4% in the industrial sector.

item.title: CME Group's International Average Daily Volume Rises 22% To 9 Million Contracts In Q3 2026
item.content:encoded:
CME Group, the world's leading derivatives marketplace, today announced it achieved international average daily volume (ADV) of 9 million contracts in Q3 2026, up 22% from a year earlier.

Reflecting all trading reported outside the United States, this volume was driven largely by growth in Energy products, up 40%, Agricultural products, up 28%, and Equity Index products, up 24%.

"Markets remained volatile in the third quarter, with geopolitical issues fueling uncertainty and stoking inflation globally," said Julie Winkler, Chief Commercial Officer at CME Group. "Against this backdrop, customers around the world turned to CME Group to manage their risk, and the growth of our international volumes was testament to that."

International trading volume expanded by at least 20% in the period in all regions including Europe, Middle East and Africa (EMEA), Asia Pacific (APAC), and Latin America.

EMEA ADV increased 20% to 6.5 million contracts driven by:-

  • Energy products ADV up 33%
  • Agricultural products ADV up 28%
  • Equity Index products ADV up 20%

APAC ADV increased by 28% to 2.1 million contracts driven by:-

  • Energy products ADV up 68%
  • Equity Index products ADV up 32%
  • Agricultural products ADV up 26%
  • Interest Rate products ADV up 24%

Canada ADV increased by 21% to 194,000 contracts driven by:-

  • Energy products ADV up 34%
  • Interest Rate products ADV up 23%
  • Equity Index products ADV up 22%

Latin America ADV increased 24% to 188,000 contracts driven by:-

  • Agricultural products ADV up 49%
  • Equity Index products ADV up 44%
  • Energy products ADV up 23%

Globally, CME Group reported an ADV of 29.4 million contracts in Q3 2026, up 16% over the same period in 2025. Q3 volumes in 2026 exceeded the prior Q3 record set in 2024. The increase in Q3 2026 ADV was largely driven by growth in Equity Index products, up 23%, and Foreign Exchange products, up 19%.

item.title: One Trading Announces Strategic Investment From Nasdaq Ventures - Nasdaq And One Trading To Explore Opportunities To Combine Their Market Infrastructure Expertise, Global Reach And Advanced Derivatives Technologies To Support Market Innovation And Enable 24/7 Trading Of Equity Futures
item.content:encoded:
One Trading, the European regulated derivatives trading venue building next-generation technology designed to support continuously operating markets, today announced a strategic investment from Nasdaq Ventures. The investment reflects Nasdaq Ventures' focus on investing in technologies that can support the continued modernization of global capital markets and establishes a foundation for Nasdaq and One Trading to explore future areas of collaboration.

One Trading’s unified deterministic trading, risk and settlement platform is designed to support cross-collateral netting, continuous settlement, and auto-liquidations at scale. This results in less locked margin and eliminates the need for a mutualized default fund. The platform combines features associated with digital asset markets, including 24/7 trading and auto-liquidations, with the protections and transparency of a regulated European trading venue.

“Nasdaq Ventures shares our belief that markets must continue to evolve to better support clients’ liquidity and capital needs,” said Joshua Barraclough, CEO of One Trading. “We believe the future of derivatives markets will be shaped by advances in technology, risk management and market infrastructure that make markets more efficient, responsive and resilient. Together, we see an opportunity to explore new approaches to derivatives innovation and help define the next generation of market infrastructure.”

Alongside the investment, Nasdaq and One Trading are exploring opportunities to bring together Nasdaq's experience in developing advanced market infrastructure, global distribution and client relationships with One Trading's cloud-deployed low-latency trading and risk engine, along with their unique regulatory position in the EU. As part of the collaboration, the companies will evaluate opportunities to modernize derivatives market infrastructure and expand the suite of products available to market participants, including long-dated futures.

"At Nasdaq Ventures, we look for teams building disruptive technologies that are uniquely positioned to expand liquidity and transparency while addressing market participants’ needs — advancing the modernization of capital markets,” said Gary Offner, Global Head of Nasdaq Ventures. “One Trading has developed a differentiated approach to integrating trading, risk management and settlement, and we believe the company is well positioned to play an important role in the evolution of derivatives markets."

item.title: SET Steps Up As “Transition Enabler” To Help Thai Firms Cut Emissions, Access Green Finance
item.content:encoded:
KEY POINTS 

  • SET advances its role as a “Transition Enabler”, supporting Thai companies to drive Thai businesses toward a low-carbon economy through the development tools and mechanisms. These include a carbon credit auction system under the Low Carbon Cities and Carbon Market Development project - expected to launch by 2027 - and the SETCarbon Platform, which enables businesses to systematically manage greenhouse gas data, enhance data credibility, and effectively develop transition plans.
  • In collaboration with Singapore Management University (SMU), SET co-hosted the Climate Finance Forum, where panelists proposed the integration of public policies, financial incentives, funding mechanisms, and climate data to accelerate the shift to net-zero emissions to accelerate the transition and achieve net-zero targets, while strengthening resilience against future climate uncertainties.

The Stock Exchange of Thailand (SET) is expanding its role as “transition enabler” supporting Thai businesses in their transition towards a low-carbon economy through the development of tools and mechanisms. These include a carbon credit auction system to support the development of the carbon market, which is expected to launch auctions in 2027, and the SETCarbon Platform, a greenhouse gas emissions data management platform designed to enhance the quality and credibility of businesses’ sustainability and greenhouse gas data. In addition, SET and Singapore Management University (SMU) co-hosted the Climate Finance Forum under Bangkok Climate Action Week 2026 on October 8 for knowledge exchange, strengthened cross-sector collaboration, and supported the development of Thailand’s climate finance ecosystem.

SET Senior Executive Vice President - Chief Strategy & Finance Officer (CSFO) Benjarong Suwankiri said: " SET's role will no longer be limited to serving as a 'capital-raising platform,’ but has expanded to becoming a 'transition enabler' that supports businesses in transitioning systematically, while strengthening their resilience in managing and responding to climate uncertainties. SET has continuously supported the development of Thailand’s climate finance ecosystem, including enhancing the credibility of sustainability data, promoting reporting and disclosure in accordance with regulatory requirements, and supporting developers of greenhouse gas reduction projects. These efforts aim to strengthen confidence among investors and stakeholders across all sectors, in line with SET's vision, 'The Trusted Gateway to Inclusive Opportunities'."

One example is the support for the development of the carbon market through the Low Carbon Cities and Carbon Market Development project, with financial support from the World Bank. The project represents an important example of how climate finance mechanisms can be applied in Thailand. It supports buildings under the Bangkok Metropolitan Administration (BMA) in improving energy efficiency. The resulting greenhouse gas emissions reductions will be registered as carbon credits and auctioned through SET’s system, with auctions expected to launch in 2027. Proceeds from the sales will provide additional funding to support the continued implementation of projects addressing climate change.

Another example is SET’s support for businesses in accessing green finance, including loans and the issuance of sustainability bonds. SET provides the necessary infrastructure to support such financing, including continuously enhanced ESG data infrastructure and the SETCarbon Platform, which helps businesses manage greenhouse gas emissions data. These are important foundations for financial institutions and lenders in assessing and allocating capital. In addition, SET has collaborated with relevant agencies, including the Department of Climate Change and Environment, the Bank of Thailand, and the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC), to develop the Thailand Taxonomy, which classifies economic activities according to their alignment with climate objectives. This helps businesses and financial institutions assess their own and their clients’ environmental performance and management, supporting transition planning, access to finance, and risk management.

At the Climate Finance Forum, panelists proposed the integration of public policies, financial incentives, funding mechanisms, and climate-related data, alongside building knowledge and capacity. Such an integrated approach would help accelerate the transition towards a low-carbon economy, support the achievement of net-zero targets, and enable Thailand to respond more effectively and tangibly to future climate-related uncertainties.

For more details on the forum and SET's sustainability updates, visit www.SETSustainability.com or follow LINE Official: @SETsustainability.

item.title: Comptroller Of The US Currency Gould Announces New Efforts To Combat Financial Fraud In Minnesota - Comptroller Affirms Support For Community Banks To Combat Fraud - Reemphasizes Banks’ Role On The Front Lines Of Protecting Consumers
item.content:encoded:
Comptroller of the Currency Jonathan V. Gould convened a panel of community bankers in Minneapolis, Minnesota, October 6 to discuss ongoing efforts to combat financial fraud.

The Comptroller’s visit supports the Trump Administration’s priority to eliminate fraud and protect Americans from illicit activity. In a discussion with local community bankers, the Comptroller discussed recent financial fraud in Minnesota, the role of banks to identify and combat fraud, and the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency’s (OCC) commitment to support banks in their efforts.

“Minnesota has seen fraud spiral out of control in recent years. Non-mortgage fraud reports in Minnesota more than doubled between 2020 and 2024, and filings of suspicious activity reports related to check fraud increased nearly 300% during that same period,” said Comptroller Gould. “Billions of dollars intended for hungry children, housing for disabled seniors, and services for children with special needs were diverted to people who cheated the system, some of whom are not even American citizens. The OCC is committed to supporting community banks in the fight against fraud and participating in a whole-of-government effort to stop those who seek to exploit the U.S. financial system or prey on American families and taxpayers.”

Click here for full details.

item.title: Nodal Exchange Achieves Growth In All Markets In September 2026
item.content:encoded:
Nodal Exchange announced growth in its power, environmental and natural gas markets in September 2026. Nodal power futures volume for September was 280,616,790, a 31% increase from the month prior. Q3 traded power futures volume totaled 693,282,299. Nodal is the #1 power futures exchange in the U.S. with 1.431 billion MWh of open interest and ~ 55% market share as of the end of September 2026. 

Environmental futures and options on Nodal Exchange posted volume in September 2026 of 67,911 lots, up 15% from a year earlier. Open interest ended the month and quarter at 461,777 lots, up 12% from a year earlier.

Renewable energy certificate (REC) futures and options posted volume of 54,997 lots in September, up 60% from a year earlier and ended the month with open interest of 377,797 lots, up 29%. In Q3, REC volume of 107,684 lots rose 21% from a year earlier.

Nodal also achieved 34% YoY growth for natural gas futures volumes for the calendar month of September. Q3 volumes totaled 297,165,000 MMBtus, a 63% increase from Q3 in 2025. Open interest reached 40,000,000 MMBtus as of the end of September, a 338% increase from a year ago.

“I am pleased to see strong performance across all of our markets for both the calendar month and the third quarter,” said Paul Cusenza, Chairman and CEO of Nodal Exchange. “We are proud to serve these markets and appreciate the ongoing support of our community.”

item.title: Alberta Securities Commission Finds That Shahin Mottahed Breached Alberta Securities Laws
item.content:encoded:
An Alberta Securities Commission (ASC) panel has found that Shahin “Sonny” Mottahed of Calgary, AB, breached Alberta securities laws.

The panel found that, while CEO of a reporting issuer formerly known as Target Capital Inc. (Target), Mottahed perpetrated a fraud on Target's investors. Between October 7, 2019 and February 9, 2021, and without the knowledge or approval of Target’s board, Mottahed diverted nearly $2.3 million from Target to Performance CBD Brands Corp. (Performance). Performance was a private business venture controlled by Mottahed, and the money was used for its benefit and that of its subsidiary, Champions + Legends Corp.

Mottahed concealed the diversion of funds from investors and the capital market by causing Target to issue false or misleading disclosure documents, including certain financial statements and news releases. Mottahed was also responsible for providing a false and misleading document to ASC staff. 

The proceeding will now move into a second phase to determine what, if any, orders for sanctions or cost recovery ought to be made against Mottahed. The timing of the next steps will be set after hearing from the parties.

A copy of the decision is available on the ASC website at asc.ca.

Allegations made against Target's former CFO, Colin Garfield Wagner, were resolved by settlement agreement in September 2025. 

The ASC is the regulatory agency responsible for administering the province's securities laws. It is entrusted with fostering a fair and efficient capital market in Alberta and with protecting investors. As a member of the Canadian Securities Administrators, the ASC works to improve, coordinate and harmonize the regulation of Canada's capital markets.

item.title: Cboe Clear Europe Expands Securities Financing Transactions Clearing Service To U.S. Equities
item.content:encoded:
• Service to expand from mid-October to include over 3,500 U.S. equities and ETFs
  • Establishes a first-of-its-kind securities lending CCP service covering European and U.S. Equities, ETFs and fixed income instruments

Cboe Global Markets, Inc. (Cboe: CBOE), a leading global markets operator and pioneer in equity and index derivatives, today announced that Cboe Clear Europe N.V., its pan-European clearing house, will expand its Securities Financing Transactions (SFT) clearing service from mid-October to include U.S. equities eligible for securities lending - another significant milestone in its strategy to expand the benefits of central clearing across the global securities lending market.

The service will initially support the clearing of SFTs for U.S. equities in the Russell 3000 Index and the top 500 U.S. listed ETFs, with plans to broaden coverage over time to Cboe's full U.S. equities trading universe of around 12,000 symbols. Settlement of U.S. securities will take place via the Depository Trust Company (DTC) in line with U.S. local best practices, with BNY acting as settlement agent. Similar to the service's approach for eligible U.S. corporate bonds and U.S. Treasuries, clearing of SFTs with U.S. equities being lent will initially be available only to non-U.S. lenders and borrowers.

Vikesh Patel, Global Head of Clearing and President, Cboe Clear Europe, said: "Expanding to offer SFTs with U.S. equities is another major step toward our vision of a global securities lending service, and underscores our commitment to delivering innovative solutions that create meaningful capital and operational efficiencies for market participants. The service's strong adoption since launch reflects the industry's growing recognition of the benefits of central clearing and our unique model. As we continue to broaden its coverage across asset classes and jurisdictions, we're helping participants optimise their securities financing activities globally, while contributing to the long-term growth, resilience and efficiency of the securities finance ecosystem."

Launched in 2025 for loans of European equities and ETFs, Cboe Clear Europe's SFT service has introduced central clearing to a market that has long operated on a bilateral basis, driving strong adoption from lenders, borrowers and agent lenders seeking the capital and operational benefits of the CCP model. Participants include many of the largest firms in the securities lending market, encompassing both UCITS and non-UCITS beneficial owners. As recently announced, the service was extended in August to include lending of fixed income instruments, such as European and U.S. government and corporate bonds, and reached a record €14 billion in outstanding loan value during September 2026.

The service provides a comprehensive solution for SFTs, covering trade matching, central clearing and post-trade lifecycle management, delivering significant capital efficiencies while streamlining settlement, reporting and client onboarding processes. Through its innovative "special clearing member" model, beneficial owner lenders, such as pension funds and UCITS, can utilise the service without posting margin or contributing to Cboe Clear Europe's default fund, helping unlock participation from all major sources of lending liquidity.

Jan Treuren, Head of Product, Cboe Clear Europe, said: "Our expansion into SFTs with U.S. equities is a direct response to client demand for a broader, globally consistent securities lending clearing solution. Working closely with market participants, we have designed the service around existing workflows, settlement practices and market conventions, making adoption as seamless as possible. The result is a solution that is designed to deliver meaningful capital, risk management and operational efficiencies while minimising disruption for our clients."

item.title: Ontario Securities Commission Publishes The RIE Division 2026 Annual Report
item.content:encoded:
The Ontario Securities Commission (OSC) has published its Registration, Inspections and Examinations (RIE) Division annual report for 2026. While this report focuses primarily on registered firms and individuals directly overseen by the OSC, firms directly overseen by CIRO and other market participants are encouraged to review the report for information and guidance that may also be relevant to them.

The report discusses important matters impacting registration, outcomes from compliance reviews, and ongoing initiatives impacting market participants.

In addition to key achievements on core operational activities, the division accomplished the following:

  • Published guidance informed by targeted reviews of Client Focused Reforms, digital engagement practices and cybersecurity controls, strengthening industry outreach and regulatory expectations.
  • Launched the division's first examinations of regulated entities and continued risk-based compliance reviews of selected CIRO dealer members in coordination with CIRO.
  • Advanced operational effectiveness through process improvements and the responsible adoption of AI to support risk-based supervision and regulatory oversight.

“Evolving markets require an equally adaptive approach to oversight." said Matthew Onyeaju, Senior Vice President, RIE, at the OSC. “This year, we strengthened our supervisory toolkit through targeted reviews, greater engagement with industry and the thoughtful adoption of technology, all while keeping investor protection at the centre of our work.”

The RIE Division is responsible for the registration and ongoing supervision of firms and individuals who are in the business of trading in, or advising on, securities or commodity futures and firms that manage investment funds in Ontario.

The mandate of the OSC is to provide protection to investors from unfair, improper or fraudulent practices, to foster fair, efficient and competitive capital markets and confidence in the capital markets, to foster capital formation, and to contribute to the stability of the financial system and the reduction of systemic risk. Investors are urged to check the registration of any persons or company offering an investment opportunity and to review the OSC investor materials available at https://www.osc.ca.

item.title: Bank Of England: Minutes Of The London FXJSC Legal Sub Committee Meeting – 16 June 2026
item.content:encoded:
The Bank of England provides the Secretariat to the London Foreign Exchange Joint Standing Committee (FXJSC) Legal Sub-Committee. The FXJSC is made up of market participants, infrastructure providers and the UK financial regulators.

Date of meeting: 16 June 2026

Time: 2pm – 3.30pm | Location: Bank of England, Threadneedle St, London, EC2R 8AH

Minutes

Item 1: Introduction

The Chair (Sharon Blackman) opened the meeting, welcoming those online and in person.

Item 2: Minutes of 17 March Legal Sub-Committee

The minutes of the meeting of 17 March 2026 were approved.

Item 3: ISDA Update – FX Definitions & Non-Deliverables (ISDA – Ann Battle and Jonathan Martin)

The discussion focused on a comprehensive update on the 2026 FX Definitions, covering the transition from the 1998 definitions, key substantive changes, SWIFT implementation, and supporting materials for firms.

Program Timeline and SWIFT Transition:

The four-year program launched in 2024 is now in implementation phase, with a SWIFT change request submitted ahead of their June 4th deadline. SWIFT rulebook changes are expected over the summer and transition to the new FX Definitions in November 2027 (after which the 1998 definitions will cease to apply).

Key Updates

  • Consolidation and Digital Publication: The 2026 FX Definitions create a single, fully digital and versioned framework that can be updated and maintained centrally, including matrix-based templates for non-deliverable transactions, simplifying operations and reducing reliance on master confirmations for vanilla trades.
  • Key Substantive Changes: Introduction of three default disruption events, alignment of the calculation agent standard with 2021 rates definitions (including a good faith/commercially reasonable standard), and optional provisions such as calendar adjustment events.
  • Business Day Framework and Automated Exercise: Streamlined and harmonised business day concept, plus a new fully automated exercise option for FX options based on published rates.
  • Implementation Materials and Outreach: A suite of materials are available and forthcoming for firms, including the FX definitions brochure, an industry implementation roadmap, a plain English guide, annotated confirmation templates, and an optional master confirmation bridge agreement. The team is coordinating with the implementation steering committee and planning dealer outreach to clients, with educational webinars and FAQs to support the transition.
  • Foreign Law Agreements and SWIFT Application: The group noted uncertainties regarding the application of the 2026 FX Definitions to non-English and non-New York law governed agreements, particularly in relation to SWIFT messaging and local banking associations.

Discussions between ISDA and local banking associations are ongoing.

Item 4: Competition Law Guidance Refresh

Non material amendments have been made to the competition law guidance. Review and comments were invited from the group, particularly to the introductory paragraph and references to the Sub Committees.

Item 5: Approval of Terms of Reference and Deputy Chair Appointment

It was noted that most substantive changes to the subcommittee terms of reference relate to the operation of the legal subcommittee and the introduction of the deputy chair role. The group was invited to provide any final comments to the Secretariat.

The Chair confirmed the appointment of the Deputy Chair (Tamsin Rolls) with no objections from the group.

Item 6: Topics for discussion at Future Meetings

The group considered revisiting legal issues relating to the use of AI in the FX markets, particularly its application in algorithmic trading and related competition law and market practices.

The upcoming policy paper on stablecoins and digital transformation was also noted, and it was suggested that the group revisit these topics once new regulatory documents are published.

Item 7: Any other business

No AOB raised.

item.title: ESMA Clarifies Access For EU Market Participants To The Services Of Third-Country CSDs
item.content:encoded:
The European Securities and Markets Authority (ESMA), the EU regulator and supervisor, has published today a statement clarifying that EU market participants should not be prevented from accessing third-country Central Securities Depositories (CSDs) beyond 17 January 2027 and until the EU finalises the legislation to extend the current transitional regime.

The current transitional regime, which allows certain third-country CSDs to provide notary and central maintenance services for financial instruments constituted under the law of an EU Member State, is set to end on 17 January 2027. 

The Market Integration and Supervision Package (MISP), currently under negotiation, proposes extending this transitional regime. ESMA understands that both the Council of the European Union and the European Parliament support an extension.

Market participants, particularly issuers, had raised concerns about the uncertainty over continued access to third-country CSD services ahead of a political agreement on the proposed legislative extension, and how this uncertainty could create operational challenges. ESMA's statement provides clarity to support the orderly functioning of EU capital markets, well ahead of the 17 January 2027 deadline.
